- If sentiment shows strong bullish (e.g., +1.00) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment shows strong bearish (e.g., -1.00), model often under-forecasts; adjust downward bias or increase early correction.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots and fails to correct — apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast growth by 10–20% in next 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00/0.25), model often drifts toward mean reversion — align forecast with recent 7–14 day moving average if no strong sentiment bias.
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from forecast in first 5–7 days (e.g., >10% deviation), model is likely lagging — adjust forecast to match recent sentiment-driven volatility.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment when it’s sparse or inconsistent — if sentiment history has 3+ consecutive 0.00 values, apply a “sentiment-weighted smoothing” rule: blend forecast with 3–5 day sentiment-adjusted average.
